title: CraigLockhart View (Edinburgh area) Wellington Memorial
memorial_type: Small concrete cairn with metal plaque detailing names of airmen
narrative: This crash involved not a routine bomber but a Wellington being used for top-secret radar research. On 14 December 1942, Wellington X3707 took off from RAF Defford in Worcestershire -- home of the Telecommunications Research Establishment, where Britain developed its airborne radar systems -- bound for RAF Turnhouse (now Edinburgh Airport). On board were four RAF crew and one American signals officer, 1st Lt Kaulis of the USAAC, reflecting the close Anglo-American collaboration on radar technology. As the aircraft approached Edinburgh it suffered engine failure. The pilot attempted an emergency landing on the allotments in the Happy Valley area of Craiglockhart, beside the Union Canal. The aircraft struck the Allan Park Bridge (now a footbridge) and burst into flames. All five crew were killed. The secret nature of the mission meant the crash received minimal contemporary publicity. Warrant Officer McFadyen and Flight Sergeant McGregor were both Scottish, buried in Glasgow and Ballingry respectively. The American officer's burial location has not been confirmed.

crew.name: Thomas Lennox French
crew.burial_location: Edinburgh (Corstorphine Hill) Cemetery, Sec B, Joint Grave 558
crew.fate_detail: Killed when Wellington X3707 struck Allan Park Bridge and burst into flames while attempting an emergency landing in the Happy Valley area of Craiglockhart.
crew.bio: A 24-year-old pilot from the RAFVR, French was flying a top-secret radar research mission from RAF Defford (home of the Telecommunications Research Establishment) to RAF Turnhouse when engine failure forced the emergency landing attempt.

crew.name: Andrew McFadyen
crew.burial_location: Glasgow (St Kentigern's) RC Cemetery, Sec 6, Grave 1776
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash. McFadyen was Scottish and was buried in Glasgow.

crew.name: Charles McGregor
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash. McGregor was Scottish and was buried in Ballingry, Fife.

crew.name: John Robert Harper
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash. As a radar operator, Harper was working with the secret airborne radar technology being developed at the Telecommunications Research Establishment.

crew.name: S. Kaulis
crew.fate_detail: Killed in the crash. Kaulis was a USAAC signals officer aboard as part of the close Anglo-American collaboration on radar technology. His burial location has not been confirmed.
crew.bio: An American signals officer from the USAAC, Kaulis's presence on the aircraft reflected the close Anglo-American wartime collaboration on radar development.

cause_of_loss: Engine failure; aircraft struck Allan Park Bridge while descending
memorial_details:
Name: Vickers Wellington X3707
Type: Cairn
Description: A small concrete cairn with a metal plaque sat at the top. Concrete bricks make up the outer facade of the cairn; the centre of the cairn is solid concrete. This plaque details the names of the airmen who perished in the plane crash.
Inscription: PLAQUE : In Memory of / [crew names inscribed on memorial] / Who tragically lost their lives when their aircraft, Vickers Wellington X3707, crashed at Craiglockhart View on14th December 1942.
Location: The memorial is situated adjacent to the bicycle lane. CraigLockhart Gardens Edinburgh City Of Edinburgh Lothian EH14 1BS Scotland
Grid Ref: NT 22596 70726
Coordinates: 55.923364324035,-3.240197926201
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/120/737/large_craiglockheart_vickers_wellington_0.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/120/738/large_craiglockheart_vickers_wellington2.jpg

The memorial, consisting of a stone cairn with an inscribed and painted metal plate on top, was unveiled on 11 November 2012.

Unveiling (11 November 2012): The memorial was unveiled to commemorate the crash of a Vickers Wellington bomber on 14 December 1942, which resulted in the deaths of the crew of five.

external_narratives.summary: Detailed account of Wellington III X3707 from the Telecommunications Research Establishment at RAF Defford. The aircraft was testing secret radar equipment when a port engine wiring fault and fuel pump defect caused engine failure. The aircraft crashed into a house garden in Craiglockhart View at approximately 11:45 on 14 December 1942.
key_details: TRE aircraft testing secret radar equipment
Port engine wiring fault near carburettor discovered
Fuel pump had foreign matter blocking delivery below 1500 RPM
Crashed into back garden of house in Craiglockhart View
external_narratives.link_description: Detailed account of Wellington III X3707's testing for secret radar equipment at RAF Defford, including an engine fault causing crash.

external_narratives.summary: Feature article in The Scotsman about the day a bomber crash-landed in Craiglockhart, Edinburgh. Covers the 2012 memorial unveiling and the history of the secret radar testing mission that ended in tragedy.
